items.item_text: Bachelors degree in Psychology, Neuroscience, Public Health, Cognitive Science, or related field (preferred)
Experience working with pediatric populations
Experience with research studies involving children, adolescents, or families (preferred)
Experience with neuroimaging research or software such as FSL, SPM, AFNI, or FreeSurfer (preferred)

The UCLA Semel Institute for Neuroscience and Human Behavior is seeking to hire a full-time Research Assistant to support the different studies, as well as additional NIH-funded research projects focused on brain development and autism. These landmark, multi-site studies aim to advance our understanding of cognitive, behavioral, and brain development through neuroimaging and comprehensive behavioral assessments. Key responsibilities:
Coordinate study visits and assist with participant scheduling and study protocol compliance
Support data collection activities, including behavioral assessments and REDCap data entry
Assist with MRI research sessions and data acquisition procedures
Perform quality control check to ensure data accuracy and completeness
Maintain study records and transfer data according to study protocols
Collaborate with UCLA investigators, staff, and partner research sites
Assist with preparation of research reports, figures, posters, and manuscripts
Support daily laboratory and administrative operations, including supply ordering and project coordination
Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and data entry systems

the final candidate who accepts an offer of employment will be required to disclose if they have been subject to any final administrative or judicial decisions within the last seven years determining that they committed any misconduct; or have filed an appeal of a finding of substantiated misconduct with a previous employer.
Familiarity with REDCap and research data management (preferred)
Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines
Ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a team environment
Strong problem-solving and critical-thinking skills
Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to interact effectively with research participants, families, and staff from diverse backgrounds
